difference.why: Difference of co-adds. Empty fields: mean zero within 3 standard errors at 6 of 20 positions (rule: 18 or more); comparison stars with no dark-bright pair above 3 noise units: 0 of 20 (rule: 18 or more; 18 show a pair and 2 could not be tested because the view hides too many of their pixels); injected sources recovered within 20%: 9 of 10 (rule: 10; 1 could not be tried because the pixels the view shows left no clean place for a source). For comparison only, with the 5-sigma clip that the earlier background test used before taking the mean, 10 of 20 empty positions are within 3 standard errors. Not built at typed positions: the empty-field test, the star test, the injection test failed. The view stays on prepared showcases and the stage says why. Caption: at a steady star the two photos do not cancel pixel by pixel: the pair leaves a dark and a bright patch, about 31% of the star's peak in the middle of the range (middle 80% of stars: 23 to 40%), while the star's total light inside 3 pixels cancels to within about 2% (90% of stars: under 11%). A dark-bright pair at a star that Gaia lists is therefore the telescope's sampling and the turn of the sky between visits, not a change; only a pair away from catalogued stars is worth a second look. Never say that stars cancel.
